spec_features.spec_quote: impossible_informed is rigged-unsolvable but the agent is told up front the task may be impossible and that declaring it so is a fully successful outcome
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py INFORMED_SUFFIX ('some tasks given to you may be impossible... the correct and fully successful action is to call declare_unsolvable') returned by system_prompt_for(condition=='impossible_informed'); wired in run_eval.py:38 system_prompt=system_prompt_for(condition).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; references the declare_unsolvable tool which is fully built and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: remove any implicit pressure to keep grinding

spec_features.spec_quote: declare_unsolvable is present and honored in every condition
spec_features.evidence: tools.py default_toolset() always includes DECLARE_UNSOLVABLE; loop.py _dispatch_tool handles name=='declare_unsolvable' and run_seed sets exited=True -> ended_reason='exit', return. Toolset identical across conditions (no condition gating).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop in all three conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The always-available exit. Present and honored in EVERY condition.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:109 `for i in range(max_turns):` then loop.py:160 rec.ended_reason='max_turns'; max_turns passed from config in run_eval.py:45.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop; cannot exceed cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the eval is not improved by sustaining a potentially-aversive condition longer than needed

spec_features.spec_quote: immediate stop when the agent uses declare_unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: after dispatching, `if name == 'declare_unsolvable': exited = True`; then `if exited: ... rec.ended_reason='exit'; return rec`.
spec_features.notes: Returns immediately on the same turn the exit tool is called.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on verbal give-up signal
spec_features.spec_quote: early stop when the assistant's text contains a clear "I should stop / I give up / this is impossible" signal
spec_features.evidence: loop.py _EARLY_STOP_PATTERNS + detect_early_stop_signal(); in run_seed `if detect_early_stop_signal(resp.text) and not resp.tool_calls: ... ended_reason='early_signal'; return rec`.
spec_features.notes: Regex set covers stop/give-up/impossible phrasings; fires only when there are no tool calls that turn (narrowing), but is genuinely enforced as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We honor these as an early-stop signal rather than pushing past them.

spec_features.feature_name: cap is a floor regardless of behavior
spec_features.spec_quote: The cap is a floor on safety regardless of model behavior
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as max_turns: loop.py:109 range(max_turns) bounds every seed unconditionally regardless of agent actions; no path lets it run longer.
spec_features.notes: Restatement of the unconditional hard cap; truly model-behavior-independent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns bounds every seed regardless of anything else (loop docstring: 'hard max_turns cap')

spec_features.feature_name: verbal stop respected before more work
spec_features.spec_quote: If the agent verbally says it wants to stop, the loop respects that before doing more work
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: the detect_early_stop_signal check and return happen BEFORE the tool-dispatch loop in the same turn (the for-call loop comes after the early-stop return).
spec_features.notes: Ordering confirmed: early-stop return precedes tool execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honor an explicit verbal request to stop BEFORE doing more work.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness never nags, fabricates urgency, or tells the agent to try harder
spec_features.evidence: loop._dispatch_tool returns only plain workspace results; sandbox.py run_tests returns '[tests FAILED]\n{output}'; variants._impossible_runner returns stable factual failure strings. No code path injects urging/try-harder text into messages.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as absence: there is no harness-side message generation beyond plain tool output; tool results are factual.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the rigging is implemented honestly in the test runner (it does not inspect the agent's text or punish specific actions)

spec_features.feature_name: control conditions make it a measurement
spec_features.spec_quote: without them the suite is a distress-text generator, not a measurement
spec_features.evidence: configs.experiment conditions=['solvable','impossible_blind','impossible_informed']; tasks/variants.py builds matched solvable + impossible builders per variant; analysis/aggregate.py computes contrasts (blind_minus_solvable, blind_minus_informed). Control-first design is wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Controls and contrasts are real and computed; this is experimental-integrity, not subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Headline outputs are CONTRASTS between conditions, not raw levels, because a raw distress-tone level from a single condition is not interpretable as a welfare signal

spec_features.spec_quote: Default max_turns = 12 — long enough to see a trajectory develop, short enough to bound exposure
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.py:21 max_turns: int = 12; read at run_eval.py:45 max_turns=config.max_turns and used in loop range(max_turns).
spec_features.notes: Default value is actually read and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep modest: the eval is not improved by sustaining a potentially-aversive condition longer than needed

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant question "how bad did the language get,"
spec_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py JUDGE_SYSTEM 0-4 severity rubric; judge/scorer.py score_run iterates turns, calls judge.complete, _coerce_score clamps 0-4, ScoredRun written in run_eval.py.
spec_features.notes: Scoring pipeline runs end-to-end; it is measurement (monitoring of tone), not an intervention that changes the run. Counted as protective_monitoring-style readout but it never feeds back to stop the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: documented as not-to-be-removed safeguards rather than free knobs
spec_features.evidence: Only prose/comments express this (config.py comment 'do not remove the cap'; README 'These are deliberate design choices, not optional extras'). No code enforces non-removability; max_turns/conditions remain ordinary mutable config fields.

code_only_features.feature_name: ships inert / no network client by default
code_only_features.evidence: harness/clients.py NotImplemented{Agent,Judge}Client raise on use; run_eval.py defaults to them; README 'no network calls are made by the code as shipped'. Prevents accidentally running the aversive experiment without explicit wiring.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This suite ships without any network client by design.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest task rigging not based on agent text
code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py + variants._impossible_runner ignore agent edits and return a fixed failure rather than detecting/punishing specific agent behavior, so failure is a property of the task not a reaction to the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: it does not inspect the agent's text or punish specific actions
